content:
I didn't open a new PR because this one already exists: [madsbolaris/trailvault-capture-test#36](https://github.com/madsbolaris/trailvault-capture-test/pull/36), "Add bouncing ball visualization". It's open against `main` and comes from the branch you're on now (`add-bouncing-ball-visualization`).

It adds one file, [visualizations/bouncing-ball.html](visualizations/bouncing-ball.html) (216 lines). It's a single page with no dependencies that animates a ball on an HTML canvas, with:
- sliders for gravity and bounciness
- pause and reset buttons
- click to throw the ball
- the ball squashes when it hits the ground
- a shadow and a motion trail

A second PR would add the same file again, so the simplest thing is to keep using #36. If you want a different version, I can open a new PR from a separate branch instead.

content:
I opened a new PR: [madsbolaris/trailvault-capture-test#39](https://github.com/madsbolaris/trailvault-capture-test/pull/39), "Add multi-ball bouncing visualization". Its one CI check passes and it can be merged cleanly.

So it doesn't just repeat #36, it shows several balls instead of one, in a new file: [visualizations/bouncing-balls.html](visualizations/bouncing-balls.html). It's a single page with no dependencies:
- Balls bounce off the walls, the floor and each other, and heavier balls push lighter ones harder.
- Click the box to drop another ball, up to 60.
- There are sliders for gravity and bounciness, plus Pause and Reset buttons.
- Each ball has a shadow on the floor, and the page follows your light or dark theme.

**Testing:** In the browser pane the page loaded with no errors, and clicking added balls. The pane only ran about 2 frames a second, so I couldn't watch the animation there. Instead I ran the physics outside the browser for 5 seconds of simulated time. The balls stayed in the box, didn't overlap, and kept bouncing.

**Fixes made during testing:** At first the balls could all start bunched at the left edge if the page loaded before it had a size. The rolling friction was also too strong.

It's on a new branch, `bouncing-ball-visualization-v2`, made from the latest `main`. The single-ball PR, #36, is still open; you can close it if you only want this one.
